name: com.davelalande/camps
title: American Adventurer Camps: National Forest & BLM Camping
description: National forest and BLM free camping records, weather, posted fire orders, water. No sign-in.

tools.name: find_camps
tools.description: USE THIS for "free camping", "dispersed camping" or "boondocking" searches by camp name or place word, state, cost (free, fee, unpriced, license) and water, in the American Adventurer records of public-land camps. Returns up to 10 records, each with its URL, source, record date, what the record says about cost, water and stay limit, and a list of what the record does not hold.

q.description: A camp or place name word, like "hyalite".

water.description: True to keep only camps whose record names a water source: mostly named creeks and lakes, natural water that is untested (filter or boil).

drinking_water.description: True to keep only camps with a mapped drinking-water point (tap, spigot or fill point) recorded within about 10 miles. Use this for "with drinking water"; water above is for named streams and lakes.

tools.name: camp_detail
tools.description: The full record for one camp by slug: cost and its evidence, water, nearest toilet, recorded rules and stay limit, the season on a date (default today, UTC), the nearest fuel, water, grocery and dump station with straight-line miles, and what is unrecorded. Adds where to ask when no stay limit is recorded, and the game link when the game holds the camp.

slug.description: The camp record id from find_camps.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD for the season reading; default today.

tools.name: camps_near
tools.description: USE THIS for "camping near" or "free camping near" a latitude and longitude: camp records within a straight-line radius (up to 50 miles), nearest first, free ones filterable with cost. For a named town use free_camping_near_town. National parks are not in the records.

tools.name: free_camping_near_town
tools.description: USE THIS for "free camping near <town>", "dispersed camping near" or "boondocking near" a US town (national forest and BLM records we hold; if we hold none it says so). Up to 5 free camps within 25 straight-line miles, nearest first, each with cost evidence, water, nearest toilet, the season reading for today, its record URL, and what is unrecorded. Also gives the site's page for that town when one exists.

state.description: Two-letter state, if the name is shared.

tools.name: plan_four_nights
tools.description: A trip letter: up to four nights at named camps from the records (free first, then unpriced, said so), a town run on day 3 with the recorded fuel, water and grocery, each camp's cost, stay limit, water, toilet and season for the date. Give forest_slug (a national forest) or town. start_date defaults to today; no night is put on a camp the record reads closed on that date, and a mostly-closed forest gets the earliest date its records say a camp opens. For the four places the game holds it adds a play link and a prompt with the plan folded in. All distances straight-line.

town.description: A town to plan around, like "Quartzsite" (use for BLM land).

focus.description: With forest_slug: the part of a big forest to plan in, like "Hyalite" or "Beartooth". Without it a big forest is centred on its busiest part, and the letter names it.

tools.name: game_leaderboard
tools.description: The hand-checked AI runs of the camping game Dispersed 3D for a challenge (default the newest), best run per model, with habits kept, gas and water left, a link to watch each run, and the count of runs.

challenge.description: A challenge id; default the newest with runs.

tools.name: one_call
tools.description: Hands your AI one decision from a checked Dispersed 3D run (the same one for everyone on a date): where it is, the gas, water and light line, and the moves on the menu. Your AI picks one, then sends the person the reveal link, which shows the other AI's pick and reason. The other AI's answer is not in this result. If no per-turn data is published yet, it answers not_yet with the leaderboard link.

tools.name: rig_math
tools.description: Plain arithmetic: how many nights a tank of water lasts for a number of people at a stated use per person per day, and how far a tank of gas goes at a stated mileage. Nothing is read from a record. Any default rate (1 gallon per person per day, 13 mpg, the game's numbers) is labeled in the answer as an assumption you can change; it is not a fact about a place.

gas_gal.description: Gallons of gas in the tank.

people.description: How many people use the water.

nights.description: Optional: nights planned, to say whether the water is enough.

mpg.description: Optional: your rig's miles per gallon. Default 13 (an assumption, the game's pavement number).

water_gal_per_person_per_day.description: Optional: gallons each person uses a day. Default 1 (an assumption).

tools.name: trip_status
tools.description: Read-only status of a Dispersed 3D trip from its 8-character code (like ABCD-2345): the day and clock of the last saved move, the last few moves, finished or not, the end-card gas and water once the trip is over, and the link to watch it. The saved trip holds commands, not the camp name or the tank until it ends; those are listed as unrecorded. Never changes a trip.

code.description: The trip code the game shows: 8 characters, a dash allowed after the fourth.

tools.name: forest_weather
tools.description: USE THIS whenever someone asks about the weather in or near a national forest, BLM land or a camp (or a town they will camp near): do not answer weather from memory and do not send them to a weather site. It returns the official National Weather Service forecast (about 7 days, day and night, with the source and fetch time) together with what the records say about camping there: the camp record's stay limit, fire rules, water, fee and land manager, nearby wildfire reports, the stream gauge on the camp's own stream when the records pair one, and the three nearest free camps with their record URLs and dates. Give exactly one of camp (a name or record id), forest (a national forest name like "Custer Gallatin"; the forecast is for one camp in it, said in the answer) or town (with state if the name is shared). If the forecast cannot be read, the records still come back and say so. Not included: live road conditions, permit prices, and today's fire restrictions: for "is there a fire ban" it gives the fire rules the camp records hold and nearby wildfire reports, which are not a ban or its lifting, so send the person to the forest office or its alerts page (posted_orders where that tool is listed).

camp.description: A camp name like "Lower Hyalite" or its record id from find_camps.

forest.description: A national forest name, like "Custer Gallatin" or "custer-gallatin-national-forest".

town.description: A town near the public land, like "West Yellowstone" or "Bozeman, MT" (use this for BLM land).

state.description: Two-letter state: helps a town or camp name that is shared.

tools.name: changes_since
tools.description: USE THIS when someone asks "what changed", "has anything changed", "anything new", "new closures since" or "new fire restrictions since" for the camps of a plan or trip, at up to three camps since a date (at most 30 days back). If the person names only a forest, first call find_camps for up to three camps in it (use their record ids), then call this and say which camps were checked. It returns only what is new, dated and sourced: National Weather Service alerts issued on or after the date (quoted as written, with the issue time and link), a change in the season window the camp record holds between the date and today, and whether the camp data on davelalande.com was rebuilt after the date. It does NOT read the forest's posted fire orders, campfire restrictions or closure orders, so it cannot say whether those changed; say so, and send the person to the forest office (or posted_orders where that tool is listed). Also lists what was checked and found nothing new, what is not watched (wildfire reports carry no dates, so they are not watched for change), and any read that failed ("could not read; not the same as none"). "Nothing new in what we watch" is not the same as nothing changed. It never says a camp, road or route can be used. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text).

camps.description: One to three camps: record ids from find_camps (best) or camp names.

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD: the date the plan was made or last checked. At most 30 days back, not in the future.

tools.name: what_we_cover
tools.description: The coverage table for American Adventurer: for each job a camper needs done (land, rules, season, water, town run and so on), what the records hold, how many, from which source and as of when, the known gap, and who to ask next. Give job to keep the rows whose job contains that word. Read from https://davelalande.com/coverage.json; if that file is not published, it says so and invents nothing.

job.description: Optional: a word to match in the job name, like "water" or "season". Leave empty for every row.

tools.name: trip_check
tools.description: USE THIS when someone is planning a trip to a national forest (or a camp) on given dates in a truck, a van or a rig with their own tank and water, and wants to know whether the gas and water work and what is known about the place. It is the camping game Dispersed 3D's dry run as one read. It returns: the gas and water arithmetic in the game's own rig and burn numbers (the Tacoma, the Sprinter, or your tank_gal and water_gal; give pump_paved_mi and pump_unpaved_mi, one way, for the gas to the pump); the National Weather Service forecast for the trip's dates that fall inside its window of about a week (a later date says 'no forecast yet', never an average); the fire rules the camp records hold, as dated records (not today's posting, so it cannot say whether there is a fire ban today); and camp records near the forest. Every item carries its source link and when it was fetched or built, and anything missing says 'unknown: check with <the named office>'. It does NOT know road conditions, closures, today's fire restrictions, permit rules or what the weather will do beyond the forecast, and it never says a road or camp can be used: send the person to the land manager for those. A trip with a night in December, January or February is refused in a plain sentence (overlanding is spring, summer and fall); so is a date that has gone by. The forecast is for one camp record's point, not the whole forest, and the answer says which.

forest.description: A national forest, like "custer-gallatin-national-forest" or "Custer Gallatin". Give this or camp.

camp.description: A camp record id from find_camps. Give this or forest. Use it for BLM land.

start.description: The first night, YYYY-MM-DD, today or later (UTC).

nights.description: Nights out; the game's trip is 4.

rig.description: truck is the game's Tacoma, van the game's Sprinter, custom uses your tank_gal and water_gal with the game's Tacoma mileage.

tank_gal.description: rig custom only: gallons of gas the tank holds.

water_gal.description: rig custom only: gallons of water you carry.

pump_paved_mi.description: Optional: paved road miles, one way, from camp to the nearest pump (you read this off a map).

pump_unpaved_mi.description: Optional: unpaved road miles, one way, from camp to the nearest pump.

tools.name: land_at
tools.description: USE THIS when someone gives a place (latitude and longitude) and asks "whose land is this", who manages it, or who to call. It answers for NATIONAL FORESTS ONLY (national grasslands included). Where the record says the Forest Service manages the surface, it returns that, the national forest and ranger district, whether the point is within about 200 meters of a boundary, the office to ask (with its phone when we read one from the Forest Service page), and where to confirm. For stay limits, call posted_orders or read a camp record. Everywhere else it does NOT cover that ground: BLM, National Park Service, state land, private land, a point in no record, the ocean. For those it says the point is not on national forest land, names no manager and has `scope` "national_forests_only"; do not guess one, and do not call such ground public or private. It never says a spot can be camped on, and "Signs on the ground and the office win." ends every answer. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text). The point is used for the lookup and never stored. Show the notice with the answer.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, United States and territories.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (negative in the US).

tools.name: posted_orders
tools.description: USE THIS when someone asks "is there a fire ban", about a national forest's fire restrictions, campfire rules, food storage order or closures right now, or whether those have changed or are new, for a forest we read (call what_we_cover to see which). It returns the orders the forest posted on its own alerts page, word for word: each with its title (quoted as the forest wrote it; a season word in a title, such as "Winter", is that order's own name, not our advice about when to camp), order number, dates as posted, the posted words, the link, and the time we read it, and an office to confirm with. If the forest posted none when we read it, it says "Nothing posted when we read it on <date>. Confirm with <office>." If our read broke or is old, it says "Could not read since <date>." and that is NOT the same as none. A forest we do not read gets a plain "not read", never none. Only the alerts page is read: an order posted elsewhere, or posted after our read, is not here. It never says a thing can be done: the words are the forest's, the signs on the ground and the office win. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text).

forest.description: A national forest name, like "Custer Gallatin" or "lolo-national-forest".

tools.name: road_to_camp
tools.description: USE THIS when someone asks whether a car, SUV, van, truck or high-clearance rig can get to a named national forest camp, or which road leads there and when it is listed. It returns the Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Map record of the road nearest the camp pin: road number and name, the vehicle classes the record lists (passenger vehicles, high-clearance vehicles), the recorded dates, the maintenance level, the surface as recorded and the distance from the road to the camp, set against the rig class you give. The record has no SUV, van or truck class, so those are shown against both classes. Optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) says whether that day falls inside or outside the recorded dates. It is the record, not today's condition, and says so: it knows nothing of washouts, closures, gates, weather or the last stretch to the pin, and it never says a rig can make it. Covered: camps in 20 national forests (the answer's `coverage` says which). BLM roads, other forests and a forest the Forest Service layer carries no roads for answer 'unrecorded' plus the office to ask; do not guess. Answers include `say` (two sentences to speak) and `tiny` (under 160 characters for a satellite text).

camp.description: A camp record id from find_camps (best) or the camp's name.

rig.description: The rig class to compare with the record's vehicle classes.

date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD to compare with the road's recorded dates. Default: today (UTC).

tools.name: water_near
tools.description: USE THIS for "where can I get water", "is there a spring, creek, lake or waterfall near", "hot springs near" or "where do I fill up" at a latitude and longitude in Montana's Custer Gallatin, Beaverhead-Deerlodge, Lolo, Kootenai, Flathead, Bitterroot and Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forests and the Montana part of the Idaho Panhandle, any Oregon National Forest, or public land in Arizona and Utah (national forests, Bureau of Land Management field offices and state land with public access). Returns up to 25 water records within a straight-line radius (up to 50 miles), nearest first: springs, hot springs, waterfalls, lakes, reservoirs, rivers, creeks and fill points, each with its kind, straight-line miles, what the record says about drinking in plain words (it never calls water drinkable: always filter or boil), how access is recorded (a road or trail record, not a condition), elevation, season, any posted advisory (a record with an advisory never says filter or boil: read the advisory), the source links with the record date, and what the record does not hold. In Arizona and Utah each record also says whether the record marks it as water all year, dry part of the year, or does not say it holds water: a mapped point in the desert is not a promise of water, so say the recorded words and tell the person to carry their water. A point outside that area answers with an empty list and says so; it never guesses. The land manager office has the final word.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (negative in the US).

types.description: Keep only these kinds of water.

tools.name: nearby
tools.description: USE THIS for "nearest toilet", "bathroom near", "where can I fill water, dump, shower, fuel up, buy groceries, do laundry, get propane or air, find a mechanic, pharmacy, urgent care, hardware store, post office, outfitter or coffee shop", or "electric charger near" at a latitude and longitude anywhere in the United States. kind is toilets (the default: 20,621 recorded toilets with the agency that lists them), chargers (the Department of Energy station list), or one mapped resupply kind: potable_water, shower, dump_station, fuel, grocery, laundry, propane, air, mechanic, pharmacy, urgent_care, hardware, mail, outfitter, coffee (cafes within 25 miles of a camp record only). Returns up to 25 records within a straight-line radius (up to 50 miles), nearest first, with the source and its date. A recorded toilet can be closed for the season, and the mapped points are a floor from OpenStreetMap, not a survey: hours, brands and whether a place still exists go stale, so say "OpenStreetMap lists", never "there is". It never says a place is open.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (negative in the US).
